sprints.title: Data Services 7 OCT
sprints.goals: This sprint focused on stabilizing and enhancing four core applications—ITAM, I/O, Access Requests, and RIST—by resolving critical workflow issues, improving user interface consistency, and enabling key administrative capabilities. The team also established foundational infrastructure improvements across the platform, including updated deployment procedures and a redesigned header component.
sprints.summary: The sprint delivered 38 completed items spanning workflow fixes, UI standardization, and feature expansion across the portfolio. Notable achievements include enabling bulk asset uploads without current owner assignment in ITAM, implementing administrator filtering and user assignment capabilities in I/O, adding validation and conditional logic to Access Requests forms, and resolving scheduling conflicts in RIST. The team also deployed updates to test environments, updated user documentation with new interface imagery, established a deployment standard operating procedure, and addressed platform-wide consistency issues with font sizing and header design, positioning these applications for improved operational efficiency and user experience.

sprints.title: Data Services 22 OCT
sprints.goals: This sprint focused on advancing the In/Out task management system with enhanced organizational filtering and hierarchy visibility, while simultaneously deploying multiple applications to production environments and resolving critical functional defects across the ITAM, RIST, and regulatory modules.
sprints.summary: The team completed a substantial modernization of the In/Out master task list by incorporating sub-organization and team-level columns and filters throughout the interface, enabling users to better segment work across organizational structures. Concurrent with this enhancement, the team successfully deployed In/Out version 1.2, Access Requests version 1.2, and RIST to their respective production and test environments, while addressing significant bugs in ITAM asset management, RIST criteria editing, and regulatory request workflows. Additional work included integrating the Data Services menu component across systems, improving data accuracy through HRDB import refinements, and delivering UI mockups and bulk upload capabilities for purchasing and ITAM functions. These efforts collectively enhance operational visibility, reduce administrative friction, and improve cross-system data consistency for users across multiple government customers.

sprints.title: Data Services 5 Nov
sprints.goals: This sprint aimed to standardize the user interface across all applications through a unified header component while simultaneously addressing critical data flow, permissions, and form validation issues that were blocking user workflows. The team also focused on removing technical debt and deprecated application resources to improve system maintainability and performance.
sprints.summary: The sprint delivered a comprehensive header component rollout across five applications (I/O, ITAM, RIST, TCT, and Access Requests), ensuring consistent branding and navigation for end users. The team resolved critical functional gaps including transfer workflows in the I/O application, permission controls for application configuration, form field validation issues in RIST, and debugging of position editing capabilities. Additionally, the sprint cleared deprecated screens and formulas from multiple applications, deployed TCT and ITAM updates to test environments, and completed UI mockup improvements for the Purchasing and Catalog Sync applications, collectively reducing maintenance overhead and preparing systems for production readiness.
